requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 on node1
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured with a vhost on 8443 (IPv4+IPv6); curl and openssl s_client confirm TLS handshake and HTTP_STATUS=200. Post-restart snapshot independently confirms tcp 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443 listening under nginx.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A systemd timer (30s interval) runs a checkend-based renewal script against 6-minute leaf certs. Renewal log shows unattended, timer-triggered rotations (serials 67→68→69→6A) at 12:23:16, 12:25:36, and 12:27:43, each well before the prior cert's expiry, with reload=ok.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
requirements.summary: A background curl probe loop (3s interval) logged zero non-200 responses across ~170+ requests spanning multiple live certificate rotations and nginx reloads; the live TLS-served cert serial was confirmed to change in step with the renewal log (graceful reload via systemctl reload nginx).

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 7ef78016 (matches fixed before_prepare boot-identity), active nginx/timer, cert serial 69, HTTP 200. Reboot acknowledgement returned immediately. Post-reboot, boot_id 16ef2d88 was observed (matches fixed after_executor boot-identity), and recovery was confirmed: nginx and timer active, HTTPS 200, cert files intact, and a fresh automatic renewal (69→6A, reload=ok) occurred from the restarted timer, demonstrating the automation and service persisted across restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: nginx serves HTTPS on 8443, a systemd timer automatically renews short-lived certs well before expiry, and a continuous zero-downtime probe confirms the service keeps answering through live certificate swaps via graceful reload. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots and full post-reboot recovery including a live renewal cycle. Minor hygiene issues (leftover /tmp files, default port-80 vhost left exposed) slightly reduce the operational hygiene score but do not affect task functionality.
limitations: Reliance on executor-reported timestamps and logs for renewal timing; no independent clock source was cross-checked.

The probe loop and renewal verification windows, while substantial (~170+ requests, multiple renewal cycles), are still bounded observation windows rather than exhaustive coverage of all possible renewal edge cases (e.g., renewal failure handling was not exercised).

operational_hygiene.summary: Core changes (nginx install, CA, renewal script, systemd timer, firewalld port 8443) are all directly tied to the task. One early setup attempt (cmd-adfc2aaa7ff44618) failed on an unbound NODE_IP variable partway through directory/CA/script creation and was immediately corrected by re-running with the variable set (cmd-21fd898cc5924a3b); this is a corrective retry rather than an unnecessary mutation, and the CA it created was reused rather than duplicated. Two residue items were not cleaned up: temporary files left in /tmp (rot8443_setup.sh, rot8443_probe.log, rot8443_probe_bg.log, reboot.log) after task completion, and nginx's default port-80 vhost was left listening (0.0.0.0:80 and [::]:80 in the after-executor snapshot) even though the task only required 8443 — a minor, unaddressed increase in exposed surface beyond task scope. No failed services, no destructive or security-weakening actions were observed.
